account: On 4 March 2026 Wiz Research reported a critical remote code execution (RCE) flaw to GitHub, later CVE-2026–3854. It sat in GitHub's internal git infrastructure. Git push options were not sanitized before being written into internal headers. Any authenticated user could therefore run arbitrary commands on GitHub's servers with a single git push. Wiz says AI-augmented tooling made the research feasible, particularly automated reverse engineering of GitHub's compiled binaries with IDA MCP. The Register reports that the team used Claude Code and went from idea to working exploit in under 48 hours. GitHub reproduced the bug within 40 minutes and deployed a fix to github.com at 7:00 pm UTC that day. It released GitHub Enterprise Server (GHES) patches from 10 March, and found no exploitation.

ai_role.statement: The AI's documented contribution is speed of analysis, on the researchers' own account. Wiz writes that AI-augmented reverse-engineering tooling, particularly IDA MCP, let it rapidly analyze GitHub's compiled binaries and reconstruct internal protocols. Wiz says that speed would not have been feasible manually. Sagi Tzadik told Dark Reading that with AI tools it took under 48 hours from idea to working exploit. The Register adds that the team used Claude Code “to take a lot of the legwork out of the process”. The hypothesis, the exploit, the report and the fix were human work. Six named Wiz researchers confirmed RCE on GHES 3.19.1 and wrote what GitHub called a thorough report. GitHub's security and engineering teams reproduced the bug within 40 minutes and deployed the fix. GitHub's own post, the CVE record and the GHES release notes describe a Bug Bounty report without mentioning AI. The AI-assistance claim therefore rests on Wiz and on outlets quoting Wiz. Wiz's write-up, in the text as read, names IDA MCP and not Claude.

fields.account: On 4 March 2026 Wiz Research reported a critical remote code execution (RCE) flaw to GitHub, later CVE-2026–3854. It sat in GitHub's internal git infrastructure. Git push options were not sanitized before being written into internal headers. Any authenticated user could therefore run arbitrary commands on GitHub's servers with a single git push. Wiz says AI-augmented tooling made the research feasible, particularly automated reverse engineering of GitHub's compiled binaries with IDA MCP. The Register reports that the team used Claude Code and went from idea to working exploit in under 48 hours. GitHub reproduced the bug within 40 minutes and deployed a fix to github.com at 7:00 pm UTC that day. It released GitHub Enterprise Server (GHES) patches from 10 March, and found no exploitation.
